subject: Prospect roles decision walkthrough — latency bands & next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Reddy <maya.reddy@medictiva.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Prospect roles decision walkthrough — latency bands & next steps

Hi Maya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a lightweight walkthrough so we can align the internal owners on your side and set expectations for procurement.

1) Who is who (what we heard)
- Economic buyer: Raj Patel (VP Product) — controls final budget/contract approval.
- Security / legal: procurement@medictiva.com + legal counsel (TBD) — will own SOC2, data residency, and encryption requirements.
- Technical evaluator: Lina Gomez (ML infra lead) — will validate latency, throughput, and deployment feasibility.
- Integration owner: DevOps team for onboarding and network tests.

Could you confirm or correct the names above? If Raj is not the econ buyer, tell me who we should loop in.

2) Decision criteria we discussed (clarify please)
- Latency targets: you mentioned p95 conversational latency targets in the ~150–250 ms range; is that for peak business hours or average?
- Cost sensitivity: you said the target is keeping inference cost to under $0.003 per 1k tokens on average — did I capture that correctly?
- Deployment mode preference: preference for Dedicated (reserved GPU) to start, with Hosted fallback for spikes. Is a Private (VPC) deployment required for procurement signoff?
- SLA: Raj indicated a desire for 99.9% uptime and an incident response playbook; would a 99.9% production SLA plus 4-hour major-incident response be acceptable?

3) Next steps (proposed)
- You confirm the econ buyer and security contact (this week).
- We send an initial Mutual Action Plan (attached) and a short SLA summary (attached) for procurement review.
- Lina runs a short validation test (we can provide a sandbox Dedicated instance) — propose a 2-week validation window.
- Internal alignment call with Raj + Lina + procurement to lock timeline (30–45 min).

Attachments: mutual-action-plan_medictiva.xlsx (MAP) and redwood-sla-coverage.pdf (summary). Ive also added a HubSpot link for the deal in related links.

If you want, Ben and Karthik can join the alignment call to cover pricing profiles and deployment options.

Thanks — looking forward to the confirmation so we can draft the MAP with clear gates.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Maya Reddy <maya.reddy@medictiva.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Ops Procurement <procurement@medictiva.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prospect roles decision walkthrough — latency bands & next steps

Vanessa — thanks for the crisp recap and attachments. A few clarifications from our side:

> On Wed, 2 Jun 2027 at 14:05, Vanessa Ortiz wrote:
> > 1) Who is who (what we heard)

Raj is the economic approver and will sign off (confirmed). Please loop him in once we have a budget estimate. Procurement (procurement@medictiva.com) handles SOC2 docs and standard T&Cs; legal counsel (Elena Wu) will be on the final redlines. Lina Gomez is correct as the technical evaluator.

> 2) Decision criteria we discussed

Latency: the p95 150–250 ms target is for interactive UI flows at typical traffic — peak hours may tolerate up to ~350 ms p95 for short bursts (not sustained). Please provide expected p95 at: baseline (non-peak), peak (business hours), and cold-starts for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Cost: the $0.003 per 1k tokens is aspirational. Procurement wants a rough monthly run-rate for 10M tokens and for a 3x peak scenario so they can compare to current vendors.

Deployment: preferred start is Dedicated (predictable performance), but procurement requires confirmation that data residency and key management meet our policy. Private/VPC would be ideal long-term but may add schedule friction; can you outline the additional lead time?

SLA: 99.9% is fine as a target. Procurement will ask for a failure credits table and an escalation path (well share their template).

I'll coordinate to get Raj and Elena on a 30-min call next week. For the validation test, Lina asked if Redwood can provide a small Dedicated sandbox with sample load scripts and an exportable latency report.

Thanks,
Maya

Maya Reddy
Head of Product Operations | Medictiva
maya.reddy@medictiva.com

Team — forwarding Maya's clarifications. Action items from my side and asks for you: 

1) Karthik: can you draft a short table for the pricing estimate (monthly run-rate) for 10M tokens and a 3x peak scenario, and include two profiles: (A) Dedicated baseline, (B) Hosted fallback for spikes? Put numbers for expected token-unit cost and an estimated monthly bill. Attach to HubSpot by EOD Monday. (related link: https://hubspot.com/deals/RW-76312)

2) Ben: procurement will need the failure credits table and our standard SLA wording plus lead times for Private/VPC. Can you pull redwood-sla-coverage.pdf (attached) and prepare an annotated version that highlights: data residency options, KMS integrations, and Private deployment lead time (estimate in weeks)? Procurement often asks for DocuSign-ready language.

3) Grace: Lina asked for a sandbox Dedicated with load scripts and an exportable latency report. Can we provision a small Dedicated pool for a 2-week validation window and provide a k6 script example? If so, include expected p95 ranges weve seen on similar customers (p95 baseline ~120–180 ms, peak ~180–320 ms depending on sequence length and batching). Note assumptions (sequence length, batching, quantization).

4) I'll coordinate scheduling with Raj and Elena for a 30-min alignment call next week — target Tue 6/8 or Wed 6/9. Maya: do either of those work?

Attachments: mutual-action-plan_medictiva.xlsx, redwood-sla-coverage.pdf (I attached the MAP and SLA summary in the original thread).

Copying the MAP link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-MAP-Medictiva
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deals/RW-76312

Thanks team — keeping this tight will help procurement evaluate quickly.

Best,
